title: Jittery batch-sampling playback sync - bench capture
content:
Context: quick sync after anomalous nightly shadow run (2026-12-07 02:00 UTC) where median token latency was normal but tail (95/99) noisier than baseline. This doc captures playback steps, observations, hypotheses, and immediate next steps.

Attendees: Evelyn (owner), Marco, Priya, Samir; notes to self: dump traces earlier next time.

Summary of reproduction:
- Test harness: bench-playback v2.3 (local capture -> playback). Config: mixed-seq (8/64/512 tokens distribution), qps target 120, continuous batching enabled, kv-cache priming ON for 75% of requests.
- Command: ./tools/bench-playback --capture=2026-12-07-shadow-001 --qps=120 --mix=0.5/0.3/0.2 --batching=continuous --kv-prime=0.75 --seed=31415
- Environment: type-d instances (A100-sim), runtime git ref: refs/heads/latency-heuristics@7f2b3d. Kernel variant: fast-attn-2.

Key observations (numbers are from aggregated run logs):
- Median per-token latency: 8.6ms (baseline 8.4ms)
- 95th percentile: 23.2ms (baseline 18.9ms)
- 99th percentile: 48.1ms (baseline 30.4ms)
- Intermittent 200-400ms spikes observed ~every 90s in host trace, correlated with GC-like memory compaction on host (syslog entries) and abrupt increase in per-GPU PCIe stall counters.
- Spike pattern changed when batch-size cap set to 32 (previously unlimited up to 128). With cap=32: 99p reduced to 35.6ms but still above baseline.
- With kv-prime toggled OFF: tail improves a bit (99p=32.0ms) implying interplay between prefix cache hit density and batching heuristics.

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Batching heuristic oscillation: workload mixes short+long sequences causing batching windows to widen and then flush irregularly; intermittent big batches cause KV cache thrash and backend stalls.
2) PCIe scheduling / host memory reclaim: guest-host memory movement spikes coincide with host-level maintenance tasks causing device stalls.
3) Kernel code path for kv-cache miss handling has a rare slow path when combined with fast-attn-2 under certain sequence lengths.
4) Observer effect: shadow run logging at high verbosity (trace-level) warmed some buffers and changed scheduling leading to spiky behavior.

Micro-checks we ran mid-meeting:
- Reduced logging level -> small improvement on 95/99 but spikes persisted.
- Forced batch cap=16 -> 99p dropped to 29.8ms; throughput dropped ~7% (qps from 120->112).
- Isolated long-seq-only run (512 tokens) -> tail stable and similar to baseline. Short-seq-only run -> tail stable. Only mixed-run causes jitter.

Unresolved questions / notes to self:
- Need trace correlation between host syslog GC entries and PCIe stall counters. Host maint tasks logged by infra? Ask infra SRE.
- Are there any pending kernel patches in fast-attn-2 that touch kv-cache path? Check PRs after 7f2b3d.
- Verify whether scheduling for continuous-batching worker threads uses backoff that can lead to bursty wake-ups when mix changes.

Immediate action items (short list):
- (Evelyn) Produce a minimal repro that flips only the batching heuristic: run with identical mix but two batching strategies (continuous vs windowed) and record traces (deadline: 2026-12-10).
- (Marco) Correlate host PCIe stall counters with infra host maintenance logs (ask infra-sre, escalate if no reply by 2026-12-11).
- (Priya) Bisect runtime ref to check for KV-cache slow-path regressions; run unit microbench for kv-lookup under our mix (deadline: 2026-12-12).
- (Samir) Run cost vs latency sweep with batch-cap 16/32/64 and collect qps/99p metrics and GPU stalls; upload CSV to /perf/artifacts/ (deadline: 2026-12-11).

Longer-term playbook ideas (brainstorm, not decided):
- Introduce adaptive batch-cap that reduces max batch size when prefix-hit variance is high.
- Add a fast-path for kv-cache sentinel misses to avoid memory compaction hot path.
- Instrument continuous-batching worker to emit micro-metrics about wake jitter and decision latency.

Meeting adjourned. Next check-in: 2026-12-11 09:00 PT (short async updates via slack).

Raw snippets / useful CLI outputs (grabbed):
- top spike sample: "2026-12-07T02:14:10Z: pci-stall-count gpu0 +37, host-mem-reclaim triggered pgcompaction"
- bench summary CSV header: time_ms,token_count,qps,median_p99,batch_size,kv_hit
- quick grep for kernel variants: git log --oneline --grep=fast-attn-2 | head -n 10

Notes: keep this doc as working capture (not final). Will update with bisect results and infra responses.
